title: Memory Model & Storage Classes
relevance: Interviewers use process layout, storage duration, linkage, and stack-vs-heap to test whether candidates can reason about C program state, bugs, and lifetimes without guessing.

phases.goal: Establish how a process’s virtual address space is partitioned and how C storage durations map onto that layout.

must_hit.point: A process gets an isolated virtual address space illusion from address zero up to the architectural maximum; every byte in RAM has a unique numeric address.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions virtual memory / per-process address space and that addresses uniquely identify RAM bytes.

must_hit.point: Typical layout has five segments: Text (read-only code), Initialized Data (explicit non-zero globals/statics), BSS (uninitialized or zero globals/statics, zeroed at startup), Heap (dynamic, grows upward), Stack (calls/locals, grows downward from a high address).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the five regions and notes heap grows up / stack grows down toward each other.

must_hit.point: The C standard defines four storage durations—Automatic, Static, Allocated, and Thread (C11 `_Thread_local`)—and never requires the words stack or heap, though compilers use them for automatic and allocated objects.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists the four durations and notes stack/heap are implementation practice, not standard vocabulary.

must_hit.point: String literals live in read-only memory (typically with/near Text), not stack or heap; modifying them is Undefined Behavior and often segfaults.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Places literals in read-only/Text-adjacent storage and flags modification as UB.

probes: Walk through where `public_count`, `pending_flags`, `local_temp`, and a `malloc`’d array live in the process address space, and why stack and heap grow toward each other.

hints.1: Think of the process like an office: code library, public globals, private locals, and a warehouse for custom-sized allocations.
hints.2: Map each object to Text / Data / BSS / Heap / Stack, and recall which end each of heap and stack starts from.
hints.3: Initialized non-zero globals → Data; zero/uninit globals → BSS; locals → stack; `malloc` → heap growing up; stack from high addresses growing down.

phases.goal: Show how storage-class specifiers, linkage, scope, and default initialization actually control lifetime and visibility.

must_hit.point: `static` means different things by placement: file-scope `static` gives internal linkage (private to the translation unit); block-scope `static` keeps local scope but changes duration to static—initialized once and retains value across calls.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts file-scope internal linkage vs block-scope persistent lifetime without calling block-scope static “constant.”

must_hit.point: Linkage: no linkage (locals), internal (`static` at file scope), external (globals/functions by default). Declare freely with `extern`, but define exactly once (ODR-style): `extern` in a header, one definition in a single `.c` file.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Distinguishes declare vs define and the header-`extern` + one-`.c`-definition pattern.

must_hit.point: Scope (where you may name it) ≠ lifetime (when the object exists): block, file, function (`goto` labels), and function-prototype scopes; a block-scope `static` can have local scope and program-long lifetime.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates spatial/lexical scope from temporal lifetime and names the four scope kinds.

must_hit.point: Default init: static/thread objects zero/`NULL` if uninitialized; automatic and allocated objects have indeterminate values if not explicitly initialized—reading an uninit automatic can be UB (trap representation) or garbage.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States zero-init for static/thread vs indeterminate for automatic/allocated, and warns about reading locals cold.

must_hit.point: `auto` is redundant for locals; `register` is a mostly obsolete register-allocation hint and forbids taking the variable’s address with `&`.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions redundancy of `auto` and that `&` is illegal on `register` objects.

probes: Explain what `static` does in `static int global_hidden` versus `static int calls` inside a function, and how that differs from linkage and from “constant.”

hints.1: Ask where the `static` appears—outside any function or inside a block.
hints.2: Outside: visibility across files (linkage). Inside: when the object is created/destroyed (duration), not whether you can assign to it.
hints.3: File-scope `static` → internal linkage; block-scope `static` → static duration, local scope, persists and is mutable; not “unchangeable.”

phases.goal: Compare stack and heap as engineering choices for where data lives and how it fails.

must_hit.point: Stack allocation is extremely fast (adjust the stack pointer) and auto-cleaned with the function, but capacity is small (often 1MB to 8MB) and overuse causes stack overflow and an immediate crash.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites speed via stack pointer, automatic cleanup, small OS-limited size, and overflow crash.

must_hit.point: Heap is slower (`malloc` bookkeeping / OS pages), lasts until `free`, can be huge (RAM/virtual memory limited), and fails via leaks or use-after-free UB if mismanaged.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts manual lifetime, larger capacity, and leak / use-after-free failure modes.

probes: When would you put a large buffer on the heap instead of as a local array, and what goes wrong if you get the choice wrong?

hints.1: Compare allocation cost and who frees the memory.
hints.2: Locals die with the frame; heap outlives the call but needs `free`.
hints.3: Huge locals risk stack overflow (often 1MB–8MB); heap is slower and leak/UAF-prone but can hold large lasting data.

phases.goal: Apply layout, duration, and linkage rules to classic bugs and multi-file / classification scenarios.

must_hit.point: Returning a pointer to a local is a critical bug: the stack frame is popped, the pointer dangles, later calls overwrite that memory, and use is Undefined Behavior.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names dangling pointer after return and UB on later access.

must_hit.point: Block-scope `static` is shared by all threads calling that function, so multithreaded use without a mutex races.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Flags shared mutable static locals across threads and need for synchronization.

must_hit.point: Classification pattern: file-scope non-`static` → static duration + external linkage; file-scope `static` → static duration + internal linkage; block automatic → automatic + no linkage; block `static` → static duration + no linkage; `malloc` object → allocated duration, no name/scope, no linkage.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Can place `alpha`/`beta`/`gamma`/`delta`/`epsilon`’s object into those buckets correctly.

probes: Why is returning `&local_temp` (or a pointer to any automatic local) unsafe, and how would you classify scope, duration, and linkage for a file-scope `static` vs a block-scope `static` vs `malloc`’d memory?

hints.1: Ask what happens to the stack frame when the function returns.
hints.2: Separate “can I name it here?” from “is the memory still alive?” and from linkage across `.c` files.
hints.3: Local’s frame is gone → dangling pointer/UB; file `static` = internal linkage + static duration; block `static` = no linkage + static duration; heap object = allocated, nameless, no linkage.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Stack: very fast (stack-pointer bump), lifetime tied to the function, auto cleanup, but small (often 1MB–8MB) and overflows crash. Heap: slower via `malloc` bookkeeping, manual `free`, can be huge, but leaks and use-after-free are UB.

gotchas.trap: Treating string literals like writable stack/heap buffers (`char *s = "Hi"; s[0] = 'h';`).
gotchas.correction: Literals live in read-only memory (typically with/near Text); modification is Undefined Behavior and often segfaults.
It means persistent: same memory cell for the whole program run, still freely modifiable, initialized once.

gotchas.trap: Using block-scope `static` state in multithreaded code without protection.
gotchas.correction: That object is shared by all threads calling the function; protect with a mutex or avoid shared mutable statics.

gotchas.trap: Reading uninitialized automatic (or assuming allocated memory is zeroed).
gotchas.correction: Only static/thread objects default to zero/`NULL`; automatic/allocated values are indeterminate—always initialize locals; trap representations can make reads UB.

gotchas.trap: Returning a pointer to a local variable.
gotchas.correction: The stack frame is invalidated on return; the pointer dangles and later use is Undefined Behavior.

gotchas.trap: Defining the same global in multiple `.c` files while sharing it.
gotchas.correction: Put `extern` declarations in a header and exactly one definition (no `extern`) in a single `.c` file.
